key_insight: A region-graph Optimal Transport (OT) routing mechanism assigns WSI patches to specialised experts, enforcing balanced and spatially coherent expert usage so Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) can better handle slide heterogeneity.
problem_solved: Standard MIL aggregators and unconstrained softmax MoE routing either force all instances through a shared pathway or produce imbalanced, spatially inconsistent expert assignments—limiting specialization and interpretability for gigapixel whole-slide image classification.
method: Build a region-graph over WSI patches to capture spatial adjacency and local context.
Use Optimal Transport to compute routing weights from regions to expert subnetworks with balance and locality constraints, preventing expert collapse and encouraging spatial coherence.
Integrate OT routing into an end-to-end Mixture-of-Experts MIL pipeline so experts specialise on distinct pathological patterns across the slide.
impact: Provides a principled routing strategy that yields more balanced, interpretable, and specialised expert pathways for WSI classification—helpful for designing robust, scalable MIL/MoE systems in computational pathology and other large-instance domains.
visual_elements: Region-graph overlay on a whole-slide image showing nodes (regions) and edges (spatial adjacency).
Sankey/flow diagram of Optimal Transport routing from regions to experts (thickness = routing weight).
Expert-specific attention maps / heatmaps illustrating spatially coherent specialist responses.
Compact pipeline diagram: patch extraction → region-graph → OT routing → expert ensemble → slide prediction.
paper_title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
paper_authors: Xin Tian, Jiuliu Lu, Ephraim Tsalik, Bart Wanders, Colleen Knoth
